Five-year-olds blamed the larger wreckage; intent only matters around eight or ten. Morality is not preloaded with an intention module; it is built up over years from outcomes first.

term: 青少年不是不懂风险，而是奖赏系统跑得比自控快
oneLiner: 认知上不输成人，但“值得吗”的算式里，“当下爽”的权重大得多。
oneLinerEn: Teens know the risks; the reward side of the equation simply outweighs them.
detail: 脑影像显示，青春期纹状体对奖赏线索的响应显著上扬，而前额叶控制要到 20 多岁才逐步跟上。Steinberg 的驾驶实验发现：单独一人时，青少年与成人的冒险决策相差无几；一旦有几个同龄伙伴旁观，青少年的冒险率飙升，成人的几乎不变。他们并非不会算风险，而是“被看着”的时候，社会奖赏的天平重重压下。理解这一点，比“再讲一遍危险”更对症。
detailEn: Striatal response to reward spikes in adolescence while prefrontal control keeps maturing into the twenties. Steinberg's driving study found teens took risks only when peers watched; alone they matched adults. The problem is not ignorance of danger but a social reward multiplier that temporarily outruns the brake.

term: 婴儿生来是「世界公民」，10 个月后耳朵开始关门
oneLiner: 6 月龄能听辨所有语言的语音差异，12 月后只保留母语的对比。
oneLinerEn: Six-month-olds hear every language contrast; a year later, only their mother tongue's.
detail: Kuhl 用“转头条件反射”测试日英婴儿对日语 /r/-/l/ 的辨别：6 月龄时，两种婴儿表现一样好；到 10–12 月，日本婴儿依旧敏锐，美国婴儿则明显退化——不是耳朵出了问题，而是大脑“用进废退”地剪掉了不常用的对比通道。这种“知觉收窄”遍布面孔、语音、音乐节奏。所谓母语，其实是一台在你身上完成第一次“版本定制”的过滤器。
detailEn: Kuhl tested Japanese and English infants on the /r/-/l/ contrast. At six months both heard it equally well; by twelve, American infants had lost the ability while Japanese kept it. Unused contrasts get pruned. Native language is not only what you learned but what you stopped being able to hear.

term: 陌生人焦虑不是「胆小」，恰恰是变聪明的信号
oneLiner: 8 月前后开始认生的孩子，在记忆与分类上往往进步得更快。
oneLinerEn: The eight-month baby who suddenly fears strangers is, ironically, maturing in memory.
detail: 陌生人焦虑（认生）在全球各文化里几乎都出现在 7–9 月。这并非“惊吓经历造成的联想”——恰恰相反，是婴儿终于形成了“熟悉 vs 陌生”的稳定分类，并对“妈妈不见了”产生了可记忆的期待。认知越成熟，认生越明显；一旦记忆系统能维持“人物-场景”的匹配模型，任何“不匹配”都会报警。所谓怕生，其实是大脑长出新软件后的一次副作用。
detailEn: Stranger anxiety arrives around seven to nine months across cultures. Bruner and Goodman read it as a sign of growing memory and categorisation: only a baby who can hold a template of 'familiar caregiver' can flag the mismatch. Fear of strangers is the byproduct of a new representational system coming online.

term: 五个月大的婴儿已经会算 1+1
oneLiner: 幕布后 1+1 显示成 3，婴儿会盯着“错答案”看更久。
oneLinerEn: Five-month-olds stare longer when 1+1 apparently equals three.
detail: Xu 与 Spelke 让 5 月龄婴儿观看“幕布后放一个 Mickey 玩偶，再放一个”的动画，然后掀开幕布分别显示 2（正确）或 3（不可能）。婴儿盯着“3”的时间显著更长——这暗示他们内部已经有一个粗略的“加法预期”。类似结果在狗、猴子、雏鸡身上也重现过。算术的雏形并非语言与学校给的，它比这些都要早得多。
detailEn: Xu and Spelke showed five-month-olds a puppet hidden behind a screen, then another added. When the screen lifted to reveal three instead of two, infants stared significantly longer, implying an internal expectation of 1+1. Comparable findings appear in dogs, monkeys and chicks. Arithmetic is scaffolded well before counting words arrive.

term: 情绪其实是身体信号的一种“解释”
oneLiner: 心跳、胃缩、脸热——大脑拿到它们后，才“贴”上情绪的名字。
oneLinerEn: Heartbeat, gut clench, warm face: feelings are the story the brain weaves over body signals.
detail: 达马西奥的“躯体标记”假说提出：情绪体验并非直接从“心”发出，而是大脑对身体状态（内脏、激素、面肌）的重新监看。他把这层“内感受”看作自我意识的地基。巴雷特进一步发现，同一股唤起在不同情境下会被“制造”成完全不同的情绪——同样是心跳加速，你完全可能把它读成“害怕”或“兴奋”。你以为你在“看世界”，其实很多时候你在读自己的心跳。
detailEn: Damasio's somatic-marker view holds that feelings are the brain's re-perception of body state—viscera, hormones, facial tension—rather than an inward broadcast. Barrett adds that the same arousal can be constructed as fear or excitement depending on context. Much of what feels like reading the world is reading your own heartbeat.

term: 工具用熟了，大脑把它“归自己”
oneLiner: 猴子拿上耙子后，视觉神经元开始把耙子当“手臂”来算。
oneLinerEn: After a monkey grasps a rake, its visual neurons start treating it as part of the arm.
detail: Iriki 等人发现，训练猴子用耙子取食物后，顶叶“手臂区”的神经元开始把工具长度编进自己的“身体图式”——对耙子尖端附近的触碰也会响应。人也一样：用棒子去戳一个物体时，大脑会把棒尖当作“你的手”的位置。身体并不是一个固定的壳，而是一个可以按需扩展的工作区。工具用得越顺手，它就越靠近“我”的定义。
detailEn: Iriki's team recorded parietal neurons in monkeys trained to use a rake. After practice, those neurons remapped to include the tool's length, treating the tip as part of the body. Human studies show a similar shift when poking with a rod. The body schema is not a fixed shell but a workspace that re-loads with each well-wielded tool.

term: 疼痛不是伤害的读数，而是大脑的“预测”
oneLiner: 组织伤不伤不直接痛，大脑先“预计你多危险”，再把痛递给你。
oneLinerEn: Pain tracks the brain's estimate of threat, not a raw readout of tissue damage.
detail: 菲尔兹长期追踪发现：战场上受伤的一半士兵不觉得痛；同一处伤在不同情绪、语言、预期下疼痛强度大不同。他提出：疼痛是大脑基于当前上下文对“组织损伤风险”的一项预测，只有当大脑判定“需要保护自己”时才会上报。慢性疼痛里，这一预测可以脱离伤害而自行持续。疼痛很真实，但它不是伤害的直接副本。
detailEn: Fields noted that about half of wounded soldiers on the battlefield reported no pain, and that identical injuries feel very different under varying context, language and expectation. He argued pain is the brain's threat prediction, delivered only when protection seems needed. In chronic pain, that prediction can persist without ongoing tissue harm.

term: 睡眠麻痹里的“入侵者”，是大脑自己派出来的
oneLiner: 身体被锁住，大脑却把自身的恐惧“外化”成一个房间里的黑影。
oneLinerEn: When the body stays locked at waking, the brain can project its alarm as a dark figure in the room.
detail: Cheyne 等人发现，睡眠麻痹中的“入侵”幻觉与心跳上升、恐惧高度相关。REM 期间被自然阻断的运动指令与正在醒来的意识错位，大脑对“动不了”作出威胁性解释，把自身的唤起“外射”成“房里有个东西”。它不是幽灵，而是一套预测、身体与唤醒系统在错误时间里拼错了一个正常现象。
detailEn: Cheyne and colleagues linked the 'intruder' hallucination of sleep paralysis to rising heart rate and fear. The atonia of REM bleeds into waking, and the brain's threat system reads the paralysis as danger—projecting an intruder that is really its own arousal mislabelled. Ghosts, it turns out, can be generated by a timing mismatch.

term: 换个身体，隐性偏见会重新“编程”
oneLiner: VR 里把“你”变成另一个种族、年龄、体型的人，几分钟后偏见就会动。
oneLinerEn: Inhabit a different-race or different-body avatar for minutes and implicit bias begins to shift.
detail: Peña 等人让白人受试在 VR 里住进一个黑人身体，几分钟后他们在内隐联想测试中的种族偏见下降，且对种族相关报道的同理上升。Slater 组也发现，把身体换成“小孩”后，受试对周围物体的距离估计会变。身体不只是“包裹思想的容器”，而是你偏见的一个可编程界面。
detailEn: Peña placed white participants in a Black virtual body for minutes; their implicit race bias dipped and their empathy toward racism news rose. Slater's group found that swapping in a child's body rescaled how far objects seemed. The body is not just packaging for the mind; it is one of the interfaces through which bias is written.

sources.label: Peña, Nussinson, Spiegel & Bargh (2013); Banakou, Groene & Slater (2013)

term: 异手症：一只手像“自己拿定了主意”
oneLiner: 它会自己解开纽扣、摸脸、甚至抢另一只手的活——而患者说“不是我干的”。
oneLinerEn: It unbuttons, gropes the face, even opposes the other hand—all while the owner insists 'that wasn't me.'
detail: Brion 与 Master 汇总的前驱病例显示：某些胼胝体或前额叶损伤后，一只手会执行看似有目的的动作（脱衣、把东西摆开），而患者会把它归为“不是我干的”——既非瘫痪，也非抽搐。它把“意志—动作—代理感”这三个平时绑在一起的链条拆开了：动作可以看似“有组织”，而“发起者感”可以缺席。
detailEn: Brion and Master's cases describe hands that unbutton shirts, fumble objects or restrain the other hand while the person disowns them. Neither paralysed nor twitching, they act with apparent purpose. Alien hand splits the usual bundle of intention, movement and sense of agency, showing that 'I did that' is an extra ingredient, not automatic.

term: 肠道里的微生物，会影响你的焦虑与情绪
oneLiner: 同样的小鼠，无菌环境里养大的胆量与“肠道居民”几乎无关。
oneLinerEn: Germ-free mice explore less than normal ones until their gut is repopulated.
detail: Cryan 与 Dinan 的回顾发现，无菌小鼠在新环境里探索更少、应激时皮质酮反应更高；把健康小鼠的粪便移植给它们后，行为会向“正常”回弹。机制候选包括迷走神经、短链脂肪酸与色氨酸代谢。这不意味着“心情不好”是“肠子的事”，但它提醒我们：所谓“心智”并不是关在颅骨里的一个模块，而是一个包括微生物在内的生态系统。
detailEn: Cryan and Dinan reviewed germ-free mice: they explored less, spiked higher stress hormones and recovered normal behaviour after faecal transplant. Vagus signalling, short-chain fatty acids and tryptophan metabolism are candidate channels. Mind is not a module sealed inside the skull; it is an ecosystem that includes your microbes.

term: 不同阵营用的是不同的“道德味蕾”
oneLiner: 自由派以“伤害/公平”为主味，保守派额外尝到“忠诚/权威/圣洁”。
oneLinerEn: Liberals season with care and fairness; conservatives add loyalty, authority and sanctity.
detail: 海特提出的“道德基础理论”把人的道德直觉拆成六个味蕾：关怀伤害、公平欺骗、忠诚背敌、权威挑战、圣洁污染、自由压迫。问卷跨文化发现，政治光谱偏左的人主要依赖前两个与最后一个，偏右的人则在六个上分布得更均匀。同一个“不道德”的词，两边人实际在指的东西完全不同。你以为你们在“争论同一件事”，其实在“吃不同的菜”。
detailEn: Haidt's Moral Foundations Theory carves intuition into six tastes: care/harm, fairness/cheating, loyalty/betrayal, authority/subversion, sanctity/degradation, liberty/oppression. Liberals weight the first and last heavily; conservatives spread across all six. Two people shouting 'immoral!' may refer to different foundations entirely.

term: 电车难题里，“亲手推”与“拉杆”走不同的脑区
oneLiner: 同一个“救 5 杀 1”，亲手推人下去会点燃情绪回路，拉杆则不会。
oneLinerEn: Pushing a person onto the track lights emotional circuits; pulling a lever does not.
detail: Greene 等人扫描受试思考电车难题：当情景需要“亲手把一个人推下”时，内侧前额叶、海马旁回与后扣带回等与情绪、个人记忆相关的脑区显著活跃；而拉杆、改道这类“非个人”情形则主要激活与认知控制相关的外侧前额叶与顶叶。同一个“功利主义”答案背后，其实走着两条不同的神经路径。“你不忍心”与“你能想”，并非同一回事。
detailEn: Greene scanned brains as people judged trolley dilemmas. Personal harm—pushing someone—lit ventromedial prefrontal and posterior cingulate regions tied to emotion and autobiographical memory. Impersonal harm—pulling a lever—engaged dorsolateral prefrontal and parietal control areas. The same utilitarian verdict travels different neural roads.

term: 情绪脑区坏了，“亲手推人”变得可以接受
oneLiner: 腹内侧前额叶伤患者，对“亲手推人”式电车情景更愿意选功利答案。
oneLinerEn: Patients with ventromedial prefrontal damage pick utilitarian answers on personal-force dilemmas.
detail: Koenigs 等人发现，腹内侧前额叶（vmPFC）损伤的患者在“亲手推人”这类个人伤害型电车难题上，更多选“可以推”；而在拉杆型非个人伤害上，他们的判断与控制组基本一致。这提一个推论：“推人不行”那种直觉，需要 vmPFC 提供的情绪信号。情绪并不是理性的干扰，它可能就是道德直觉本身的零件。
detailEn: Koenigs tested patients with ventromedial prefrontal lesions on trolley cases. On personal-force dilemmas (push a man), they chose the utilitarian option far more often than controls; on lever cases they matched controls. Moral 'no' to pushing seems to depend on an affective signal vmPFC contributes.

term: 人愿意花钱去罚一个与自己无关的不公
oneLiner: 旁观者可以“自损一百，他损一千”，只为让不公平的分配者付出代价。
oneLinerEn: Bystanders will pay to punish an unfair splitter even when the loss costs them too.
detail: Feinberg 等人在“最后通牒博弈”里让受试既可选择接受不公平分配、也可以花自己的钱惩罚对方。大多数人愿意“自损”去罚“分得太多”的对手，即使两人将来再也不会见面。这种无回报的惩罚在其他灵长类里很难重现，被认为是人类维持合作的一种“昂贵但有效”的机制。你以为是你在“主持正义”，其实是演化把你塑成了一个不惜自损的执法者。
detailEn: In ultimatum games, people pay their own money to punish a splitter who treated them unfairly, even when the pair will never meet again. Feinberg and colleagues read this 'altruistic punishment'—rare in other primates—as an expensive glue for human cooperation. The urge to 'be fair' is not just principle; it is a costly enforcement circuit built into us.

term: 看别人做好事，胸口会“暖”一下
oneLiner: 目暏善行会引发独特的心口发热与“想多做好事”的冲动。
oneLinerEn: Watching virtue can warm the chest and spark an urge to do more good yourself.
detail: 海特区分了“elevation”与普通的快乐或感动：受试看完“人性光明面”的纪录片后，更多报告胸口发热、喉部发紧、想帮助他人。这个情绪不像“恐惧”一样把身体拉回自卫，而把“我想成为一个更好的人”的动机推上前台。它提醒我们：道德不只是“不能做什么”，也是一套把身体点燃、想向前行的情感系统。
detailEn: Haidt isolated elevation from generic warmth: after films of moral beauty, people reported chest warmness, throat tightness and a want to help. Unlike fear's self-defence, elevation seems to prime 'I want to be better.' Morality is not only prohibition; it is also a body-level ignition toward virtue.

term: 你以为是“人性”的东西，其实很 WEIRD
oneLiner: 心理学论文 80% 以上来自西方教育工业化富裕民主国家，却常被当作“人类”结果。
oneLinerEn: Most findings rest on Western, Educated, Industrialised, Rich, Democratic samples yet get reported as human nature.
detail: Henrich 等人发现，WEIRD 人群在视觉错觉、公平偏好、推理任务与道德判断上都显著偏离全球分布——他们是“最奇怪的 5%”。所谓“自然”的个体主义与抽象道德规则，其实与传教士、法治与学校系统长期相关。把 WEIRD 当默认“人类”，就像把哈佛本科生当全人类。一个“普遍”的心理学结论，需要先问：它在哪群人里成立？
detailEn: Henrich and colleagues showed WEIRD samples sit at the extreme edge of human variation—on optical illusions, fairness, reasoning and moral judgements. Their 'universal' individualism is historically tied to missions, courts and schooling. Treating WEIRD findings as human defaults mistakes Harvard undergraduates for the species.

term: 一旦被“多少钱”提问，神圣价值会令人发怒
oneLiner: 把“能不能卖国”换成“多少钱可以”，回答会瞬间变成长期“不可交易！”。
oneLinerEn: Ask 'how much would you accept to sell X?' and a value flips from trade-off to outrage.
detail: Tetlock 发现，一旦把神圣议题（比如选票、器官、言论自由）翻译成定价问题，人们会出现近乎身体性的反感：“这不是能算的事”。有趣地，同一群人在“为了正义，多少代价也可以”一侧也同样容易走极端。神圣价值不只是一个“很强的重要”，而是把一件事从“权衡”领域拉进了“禁忌”领域——一旦进入，任何价格提问都看起来像不敬。
detailEn: Tetlock showed that pricing a sacred value (a vote, a kidney, free speech) triggers moral outrage: 'these things are not for sale.' The same people also endorse extreme costs when fighting 'for' a sacred value. Sacredness is not just weight; it moves an item out of trade-off arithmetic altogether.

term: 好奇不是“想知道”，是一种“信息缺口”的疼
oneLiner: 好奇的强度不取决于知识多少，而取决于你知道与想知道之间的缝。
oneLinerEn: Curiosity scales with the gap between what you know and what you want to know.
detail: 罗文斯滕把好奇重定义成一种“剥夺状态”：当你知道自己“应该知道但不知道”那一小块时，心理痒感把你推向信息。这个定义解释了两个反常现象：专家对新信息更饿（因为他们能看见自己的缺）；完全无知的初学者反而不“好奇”。广告、标题党、悬念叙事的钩子都基于同一个原理——先让你“看见自己的缺口”。
detailEn: Loewenstein recast curiosity as a deprivation state: you itch when you notice a specific gap between what you know and what you want to know. Experts are hungrier because they can see their own gaps; total novices often feel none. Cliffhangers and clickbait monetise the same principle—first make the hole visible.

term: 越被禁止，越想做：心理反抗
oneLiner: “不许碰”三个字，比“碰了会痛”更能驱动你去碰。
oneLinerEn: 'Do not touch' out-drives 'touching hurts' at pulling the hand toward it.
detail: Brehm 提出：一旦你感到“我的自由选择权”被限制，会不顾代价地重新拿回它——即使原本你对那件事本没兴趣。他的“禁书实验”中，被标为“仅限特定人群”的书册，反而被受试评为更有吸引力。这也是为什么“劝退”常常适得其反，“逆反”不只属于青少年。对自由的意识非常脆弱，一句“不许”就足以把它擕动。
detailEn: Brehm proposed that when a freedom feels restricted, people reassert it at cost, even for options they did not previously want. His 'forbidden books' study showed that shunting a book behind a 'restricted' sign raised its appeal. Reactance explains why 'do not' often outperforms 'this will hurt you' at pulling the hand.

term: 事先“找好退路”，赢了风光输了不丑
oneLiner: 重要考试前一晚不复习而打游戏——为的不是快乐，而是面子。
oneLinerEn: Skipping study before a big exam is often a hedge to protect the self-image, not a bid for fun.
detail: Jones 与 Berglas 发现，人在预期自己会失败时，会主动制造障碍（喝酒、不睡、不练），为自己预先准备好一个“外部归因”。输了，可以说“我今天状态不好”；赢了，则是“没准备也能行”。它把“自我价值”从“我能力到底行不行”里隔开了。代价是：你为了保住面子，把真正可以变强的机会先拆掉一半。
detailEn: Jones and Berglas showed that people expecting failure sometimes plant obstacles the night before—drinking, staying up, skipping practice—to have an external excuse ready. Losing becomes 'I was hungover'; winning becomes 'I did it anyway.' The self-image is protected; the opportunity to actually improve is half-sacrificed.

term: 越费劲得到的，你越把它说得值得
oneLiner: 入了一个“需痛”的会，人会自动把它说得更有意思。
oneLinerEn: Endure an initiation ritual and the group's rating rises to match the pain.
detail: Aronson 与 Mills 让女生经历一段“尴尬到痛”的入会仪式后评价讨论内容；体验过痛的那组把无意义的讨论评得明显更有趣。因为“我自愿受了痛 → 目标必须值得”不能同时发生冲突，认知失调会把“目的的价值”往上推。这个机制不只存在于邪教入会：高强度训练、长期加班、难考的证书，都会因你的付出而被事后美化。
detailEn: Aronson and Mills had women endure an awkward initiation before joining a discussion; those who suffered rated the (deliberately dull) talk as far more interesting. 'I chose this pain, so the goal must be worthy' resolves dissonance by inflating the value of what was earned. Hard entry, long hours and painful certifications gain their sheen partly from what they cost.

term: 把目标说出来，反而容易口头“完成”
oneLiner: 当众宣告“我要考研”后，大脑会先“预发”一份成就感。
oneLinerEn: Announcing a goal lets the brain cash in a slice of the identity before any work.
detail: 戈尔维策等人发现，当受试对同学宣告“我要成为律师”后，他们在相关任务上坚持的时间反而更短——因为宣告已让大脑先“尝”到了一部分身份实现的满足。社会认可把“成为”提前“完成”了。一个反直觉的推论：真正想变强的人，少把目标当社交货币。
detailEn: Gollwitzer and colleagues found that participants who announced an identity goal to peers stuck with related tasks for less time. The public claim let the brain bank a slice of the achievement in advance. Turning goals into social currency can quietly cash them out before the work begins.

sources.label: Gollwitzer, Heckel & Stahlberg (2010); Park, Aldrich & Gollwitzer (2009)

term: 多巴胺不编“快乐”，它编“意外”
oneLiner: 拿到预期的奖励不会多一奖；意外的好运才是多巴胺高峰。
oneLinerEn: Expected rewards do not spike dopamine; a surprise win does.
detail: Schultz 的猴子实验发现，多巴胺神经元的放电并不对应“有汁”，而对应“比预期多”的汁。完全预测到的奖励不会提升信号；预期落空时信号反而下降。这重新定义了“上瘾”：你不是爱上了毒品或赌博本身，而是爱上了它们提供的高预测误差。一旦奖励变得“完全可以预期”，多巴胺便抽身而去——这是“到手就后悔”的神经机制。
detailEn: Schultz recorded dopamine neurons in monkeys: they fired not to juice but to juice that exceeded expectations. Fully predicted rewards produced no bump; omitted ones dropped the signal. This reframes addiction: what hooks you is not the prize but its prediction error. Once the reward becomes fully expected, dopamine moves on.

term: 时间地标：新年、生日、周一，都是重启按钮
oneLiner: “从下周一开始”不是拖延，是大脑真正的重启机制。
oneLinerEn: 'Start next Monday' is not mere procrastination but a real psychological refresh button.
detail: 米尔克曼等人发现，人们在新年、生日、月末、甚至“开始新工作那一周”这类时间地标之后，健身、学习、不抽烟等目标行为会短暂上升。地标把“旧我”与“新我”切开，“失败”属于上一个心理单元，新单元里你又是干净的。了解这一点的人，会主动利用周一、月初、入学、入职作为自己的“合法重启”，而不必等到“从明天开始”。
detailEn: Milkman and colleagues showed that behaviour change clusters after temporal landmarks—New Year, birthdays, month ends, the first week of a new job. A landmark partitions 'old me' from 'new me,' quarantining failure in the previous psychological unit. Strategic people harvest these resets rather than wait for an imagined 'tomorrow.'

term: 你大脑里 47% 的时间不在当下，而且它常让你不快乐
termEn: A Wandering Mind Is an Unhappy Mind
oneLiner: “神游”不是休息，它多发生在不想做的事里，且与当下不快乐相关。
oneLinerEn: Mind-wandering is not rest; it often drifts during unwanted tasks and tracks with lower happiness.
detail: Killingsworth 与 Gilbert 用手机抽样 2000 多人的日常体验，发现他们几乎 47% 的时间在想“不在眼前的事”。更关键的是：神游与当下的不快乐同现，而且方向常常是“先不快乐、后神游”——而不是“神游带来快乐”。大脑一边处理手头，一边一直在开“另一个频道”；你以为的“默认”其实很贵。
detailEn: Killingsworth and Gilbert sampled over 2,000 people's moment-to-moment experience. Nearly 47% was spent on something other than what was at hand, and such wandering tracked with lower happiness. Direction analysis suggested unhappiness prompted wandering rather than the reverse. The mind's 'second channel' costs more than it pays.

term: 任务“难”到一定程度，分心物自动看不见
oneLiner: 不是“意志力”让你不听旁白，而是任务真的把处理带宽占干了。
oneLinerEn: When a task eats real bandwidth, distractors drop out before awareness.
detail: 拉维提出：“选择注意”并不完全由你的意志决定，而取决于任务的“知觉负荷”。负荷高时，有限的处理资源被当前任务吃光，分心物“连抵达意识的门票”都拿不到；负荷低时，剩余资源会自动向外溢出——那时你才真的会被旁白干扰。同一个“专心”，在不同负荷里，是两种完全不同的机制。
detailEn: Lavie's load theory holds that selectivity is not purely a matter of will. Under high perceptual load, distractors fail to reach awareness because processing capacity is spent on the task; under low load, spare capacity spills outward and intrusion happens. 'Concentration' is two different machines depending on task load.

term: 你能同时“数住”的物体，大概只有四个
oneLiner: 不数数、只盯目标，大多数成年人的上限在 4 个左右。
oneLinerEn: Without counting, most adults track around four moving targets at once.
detail: Pylyshyn 与 Storm 发明“多物体跟踪”任务：屏幕上若干个圆盘，一部分闪一下作为“目标”，之后全部随机运动；受试不能说“刚才那个”——因为所有圆盘都长一样，只能“盯住”。结果发现：不靠语言与策略的“对象文件系统”上限约 4 个。你平时以为自己在“看全盘”，其实只是在几个标签之间来回盯。
detailEn: Pylyshyn and Storm asked people to track several identical discs marked briefly as targets that then moved randomly. Without verbal labels or strategies, capacity tops out near four. The feeling of 'watching everything' is really a handful of object-files kept alive in parallel.

term: 一声“叮”，能让一闪光看成两闪
oneLiner: 视觉被听觉改写：声音多一个，你看见的光点就会“变多”。
oneLinerEn: Add a beep and a single flash looks like two: hearing overwrites vision.
detail: Shams 等人发现，向受试同时提供一闪与两声“叮”，不少受试会看见两闪。大脑不将视觉、听觉分开处理，而是默认“同一时刻发生的事很可能同一来源”，并把它们“绑”成一个事件。你以为自己在“看”，其实很多时候你在听。“知觉”不是五个独立传感器，而是一个默认建“事件”的解释器。
detailEn: Shams paired one visual flash with two beeps; many people reported two flashes. The brain assumes co-occurring signals share one cause and merges them. What feels like 'seeing' is often a multisensory inference: perception builds events, not sensor readings.

term: 换个人说话，你几乎听不出来
oneLiner: “变化盲视”不只发生在眼里，它在耳朵里叫“变化聋”。
oneLinerEn: The audio cousin of change blindness: swap the speaker mid-sentence and listeners miss it.
detail: Simons 与 Levin 在电话语音实验中慢慢变换说话人（性别、音高、甚至语言），多数人察觉不到。只有当你注意“到底谁在说”时，听觉才会开启差异监测。否则，“听到”的只是语义内容，而声纹被当作“不重要”的字段默认忽略。你以为你在“听人”，其实你主要在“听信息”。
detailEn: Simons and Levin swapped a speaker's voice mid-phone-call—even across gender and language—and most listeners did not notice. Unless you track who is speaking, the audio stream is parsed for content and the speaker field goes unread.

term: 双耳分听：“另一只耳朵”里的内容几乎全丢
oneLiner: 两只耳朵听到不同句子时，未注意那只里的内容几乎不会进入意识。
oneLinerEn: Attend one ear and the other's words slip past awareness almost entirely.
detail: Cherry 经典“双耳分听”实验中，受试一只耳听英语、一只耳听德语，被要求只复述英语那侧。结束后，他们几乎无法报告另一耳里“从英语换成了德语”、“从男声换成女声”，甚至“句子倒着播放”——只有音调、扬声器位置这类“物理”属性会漏上来。“鸡尾酒会效应”能听到名字，“双耳分听”则证明名字以外的大多数声音都会被过滤。
detailEn: Cherry fed one ear English and the other German and asked participants to shadow only the English side. Few could report that the ignored channel had switched language, gender or even played backwards. Only physical attributes—pitch, speaker location—leaked through. Attention filters far more than the cocktail-party effect suggests.

term: 梦中知道自己在做梦：清明梦可以训练
oneLiner: 大脑能一边做梦，一边保持“我在做梦”的元认知。
oneLinerEn: The brain can run a dream and still hold the thought 'I am dreaming.'
detail: 拉伯格用预先约定好的眼球信号（REM 时眼外肌仍可用）确认：受试能在梦里“报信”，且报告里对梦内容的控制与自我反思显著上升。后续实验发现，训练“现实检验”（白天反复问自己“我在做梦吗”）能提升清明梦频率。它拆开了两个直觉：“梦”与“意识”不是天然对立；“元认知”也不只在醒着时上线。
detailEn: LaBerge pre-arranged eye-movement codes—usable during REM—to prove that subjects could signal from within dreams while reporting awareness of dreaming. Reality-check training raises lucid frequency. Dreaming and consciousness are not opposites, and metacognition can run during sleep.

term: 大脑“空闲”时，其实在忙“我”的故事
oneLiner: 不专注外部任务时的“默认网络”，与自我参照、回忆与未来想象高度重叠。
oneLinerEn: The 'idle' brain runs a self-story: memory, projection and identity share its default network.
detail: Raichle 等人发现，当受试“什么都不做”时，内前额叶、后扣带回与角回等区域反而活动上升——他们称之为“默认模式网络”。后续工作发现，这个网络高度参与自我参照、回忆过去与想象未来。阿尔茨海默与抑郁症中，它也是异常的中心。大脑从没有真正“闲着”，它只是换了一个频道：“我”。
detailEn: Raichle's group found that apparent rest lights ventromedial prefrontal, posterior cingulate and angular regions—the default mode network. It tracks self-reference, episodic memory and future thinking, and misfires in depression and Alzheimer's. The brain never idles; it just switches channel to 'me.'

term: 全麻不是“睡着了”，而是大脑整合能力被断开
oneLiner: 麻醉下的脑电仍可波动，但前后区域不再“对话”。
oneLinerEn: Even under anaesthesia the cortex still fires, but front and back stop talking to each other.
detail: Mashour、Alkire 与 Brown 的回顾提出：意识并不对应“大脑开/关”，而依赖于长距离信息整合。全麻时，前额叶与后部皮层之间的互联显著下降，脑电呈“前向反馈丢失”的形态。一些受试在手术中仍有局部听觉反应，但意识不“拼”起来。一个推论：“醒着”不是一个开关，而是一种“互联拓扑”。
detailEn: Mashour, Alkire and Brown argue that consciousness is not a global switch but a pattern of long-range integration. Under general anaesthesia, front-back connectivity collapses, EEG shows anterior-to-posterior signalling failure, and the 'self' fails to assemble even as local regions remain active.

term: “灵魂出窍”可以被颞顶叶电极“打开”
oneLiner: 轻轻电流颞顶叶，患者会飘到天花板上看自己。
oneLinerEn: A mild current at the temporo-parietal junction can lift a patient to the ceiling to watch their own body.
detail: 布兰克（Blanke）组在颅内电极定位癫痫时偶然发现：右侧颞顶叶交界处受到刺激时，患者会报告“自己飘到天花板上看床上的身体”，身体图式与视角自动错位。断开刺激后体验立刻消失。“自我位于身体内”不是一个不可违抗的直觉，而是一套可以被电信号“临时改写”的多感官整合。
detailEn: Blanke and colleagues found that stimulating the right temporo-parietal junction during epilepsy mapping caused patients to float up and look down on their own body. Cutting the current restored self-location. Being 'inside' your body is a multisensory construction, editable by electrodes.

term: 意识可能是大脑的“全局广播”
oneLiner: 一个信号只有被“广播”到全脑多个区域，才可能被意识到。
oneLinerEn: A signal becomes conscious when it is broadcast widely across front and back cortical hubs.
detail: Dehaene 与 Changeux 的“全局工作空间”模型主张：大脑里无意识处理器同时在跑，只有当一个信息进入前-后额叶长距网络的“全局广播”时，它才变得“被意识到”。这个框架把盲视、注意瞬脱、双耳分听与全麻归入同一个直觉：“你没意识到”≠“没处理”，而是“没上线广播”。
detailEn: Dehaene's global-workspace model holds that the cortex runs many parallel processors, and a signal is 'conscious' when it ignites a long-range front-parietal broadcast. Blindsight, blink, dichotic listening and anaesthesia all read as failures of broadcast rather than failures of processing.

term: 混着学比一类一类似块学更牢
oneLiner: 把 A/B/C 交替排，比 AAA→BBB→CCC 当场“看起来”差、考得好。
oneLinerEn: Mixing A/B/C feels worse in practice but scores better later than A-A-A, B-B-B, C-C-C.
detail: Rohrer 与 Taylor 让学面积公式的学生采用两种安排：一个类似块练习、一个交替排序。前者当场练得更多、后者练得慢——但一周后考试，交替组的成绩提升两倍。机制候选：交替迫使大脑不断“重新提题目”，而不是“沿上一次思路”干。学得很顺时，你可能只是在“同一块缓存里”反复取。
detailEn: Rohrer and Taylor had students practise volume formulas in either blocked or interleaved order. Blocked learners looked better in the session; interleaved learners doubled their scores a week later. Mixing forces retrieval and discrimination rather than riding the previous mental groove.

term: “先失败再听讲”，比直接听讲记得更牢
oneLiner: 让学生先自己探索错误方法，后接老师讲授，反而推高理解与迁移。
oneLinerEn: Struggling first, then receiving instruction, raises both understanding and transfer.
detail: Kapur 在印度与澳洲数学课上发现，让学生先挑战一个“他们不会”的题目（他们产出很多错方法），再讲授标准解，他们在延迟考试上的理解与迁移都胜过“先听讲后练”的对照组。失败不是学习的反面，而是为后续讲授“预开”多个可连接的钩子——“我试过的”比“被告知的”更容易被重新拾起。
detailEn: Kapur gave students an unsolvable-by-them problem first, then taught the standard method. Their delayed-test understanding and transfer beat the 'lecture first, practise later' control. Failure primes future instruction by pre-opening hooks: 'what I tried' is easier to reactivate than 'what I was told.'

term: 先考后学，即使答错也让你记得更多
oneLiner: 预先猜错一个答案，反而把后面正确内容的“记得牢”拉高。
oneLinerEn: Guessing wrong before reading a passage helps the right answer stick later.
detail: Kornell、Hays 与 Bjork 让受试先猜与答案无关的词（注定错），再阅读词条。直接阅读组在延迟测试上明显记得更少。一个解释：先猜会启动“注意力差异信号”，把后面正确内容标成“与我的预期不同”，而“不同”在记忆里天然重要。一个反直觉推论：学习开始时，先提“不会也硬猜”的问题。
detailEn: Kornell, Hays and Bjork had people guess (wrongly) before reading glossary entries. Pretesting boosted later retention compared with reading only. Generating an answer, even a wrong one, marks what follows as a prediction error, and the brain privileges 'different from expected.'

term: “再读一遍”几乎无效，但大脑会“报信错”
termEn: Rereading Feels Better Than It Works
oneLiner: 重读带来“很顺”的流畅感，却被大脑误读成“已经掌握”。
oneLinerEn: Fluency on a second pass is mistaken by the brain for mastery.
detail: Karpicke 与 Roediger 发现，阅读同一段落 4 遍的人与读 1 遍后测试 3 次的人相比，当下都觉得自己“读4遍那组学得多”——但一周后，后者记得更多。重读把“文本熟悉”误报为“知识掌握”，属于元认知判断的失败。考试前“翻书”的安心感，很大一部分只在“眼睛很熟”，而不在“能产出”。
detailEn: Karpicke and Roediger compared reading a passage four times versus reading once and self-testing three times. Rereaders felt more confident yet remembered less a week later. Perceptual fluency masquerades as mastery: the eye's familiarity becomes the mind's misplaced confidence.

term: “为什么这一步成立？”——自己给自己解释，提升学习
oneLiner: 高绩效学生与同学的差距，不在看了什么，而在“一路小声追问为什么”。
oneLinerEn: The best learners are not watching more; they are asking 'why does that step hold?' as they read.
detail: Chi 等人对比学生学牛顿力学时的自我报告：高手会不时停下“给自己”解释为什么下一步成立，并将新内容与旧知识重新接线；新手一路读下去、少停下来追问。后续课堂实验发现，被提示“每段后写下为什么”的新手，也能接近高手成绩。“元认知”不只是“知道自己不知道”，而是把“知道”一步一步写下来。
detailEn: Chi's protocol analysis showed that strong learners paused mid-solution to explain each step to themselves and to connect new claims to prior knowledge; weak learners read on. Students prompted to write 'why' after each paragraph gained comparable performance, elevating metacognition to an active habit.

term: 偏见盲点：别人的偏差一眼看穿，自己的看不见
oneLiner: 人能识别十几种认知偏差在自己身上的缺失。
oneLinerEn: People spot every bias in others—except the one they are running right now.
detail: 普洛宁等人发现：受试能承认“人类”很容易受刻板印象、确认偏误、错误共识影响，但一谈到自己，就默认“我大概例外”。更反常的是，越是“看见”自己有某种偏差的人，越认为自己在其他事上更客观——这本身又成了一道新偏差。元认知能监控很多事，但对“监控自己的监控”几乎不提供接口。
detailEn: Pronin and colleagues found that people readily admit humans fall prey to stereotypes, confirmation bias and false consensus, but assume they themselves are roughly exempt. Ironically, those who spot more bias in themselves claim greater objectivity on other matters—opening a second-order blind spot.

term: “读得顺”≠“记得住”：学习判断被流畅感骗了
oneLiner: 你预测自己“下次能不能想起”，用的线索只是“这次读得顺不顺”。
oneLinerEn: Predictions of later recall lean on how smoothly a page reads now, not on how deeply it encoded.
detail: 克里亚特系列实验发现，人对自己“下次能不能回忆”的预测（JOL）受字体、重复、语义流畅度影响很大——而与未来真实回忆量并不同步。一个直接推论：“学会了”的感觉，并不是一个可靠的信号；它只是当前处理难度的“读数”。想拿到真实的预测，只能把“合上书自己写下来”作为反馈。
detailEn: Koriat showed that judgements of learning (JOL) track cues like font, repetition and reading fluency more than actual future recall. The feeling 'I know this' is largely a readout of present ease. The only reliable calibrator is to close the book and generate the answer from memory.

term: 把自己的直觉测两次取平均，往往更准
oneLiner: “群体智慧”不只存在于人群，也可以在你自己的两次直觉之间。
oneLinerEn: Wisdom of crowds works at the level of one person: two independent guesses beat either alone.
detail: 黑尔措希与尔特威格发现：同一个人独立给出两个估计（隔一段时间、换一种提问方式），取平均值后误差会显著下降，提升幅度接近“向另一个人再要一个估计”。我们习惯把“直觉”当作单一信号，但它更像“带噪采样”——多取几次、把它们平均，相当于“借”一点别人的智慧。
detailEn: Herzog and Hertwig showed that averaging two of a person's own estimates—taken with delay or a rephrased prompt—cuts error almost as much as averaging with another stranger's. Intuitions are noisy samples; drawing more of your own gets you part of the crowd's wisdom for free.

term: 什么时候可以相信专家的直觉？
termEn: When Expert Intuition Can Be Trusted
oneLiner: “专家直觉”并非全不可信，但它需要两个苛刻条件同时成立。
oneLinerEn: Expert intuition earns trust only in environments that are both high-validity and long-practised with feedback.
detail: 卡尼曼与克莱因罕见联名：直觉在消防、国际象棋、肌肉医生这类“规律稳定 + 即时反馈 + 长期练习”的领域可靠；而在临床心理诊断、股票预测、长期政治预测这类“低效度”环境里，专家直觉与随机接近。“专家直觉”不是一个可全局信任的黑箱，它只在特定生态位里被驯化。
detailEn: Kahneman and Klein's joint paper argued that intuitive expertise deserves trust in high-validity, feedback-rich fields (firefighters, chess masters, anaesthesiologists) but not in low-validity prediction domains such as clinical judgement or stock picking. Intuition is a trained instrument, only in certain environments.

term: 冒名顶替感：把成功归给“时机”，把失败归给“自己”
oneLiner: 越是优秀的人，越容易把成就解释成“他们还没拆穿我”。
oneLinerEn: High achievers often read their wins as luck and their slips as the truth leaking out.
detail: 1978 年 Clance 与 Imes 在大学高成就女性中发现一种反复出现的体验：把成功归因于运气、时机或别人的误判，把失败归因于能力。后续回顾（Bravata 等 2013）显示，它在博士生、博士后、教授、创业者中都普遍存在，男女比例接近。它并不是“谦虚”，而是一种稳定的归因风格：正面证据被解释成“例外”，负面证据被解释成“我原形”。所谓“成熟”，很多时候只是第一次允许自己把成功算进自己。
detailEn: Clance and Imes named the pattern in high-achieving college women: wins get attributed to luck or others' misjudgement, setbacks to personal inadequacy. Bravata's 2013 review found it common among graduate students, postdocs, professors and founders at roughly similar rates in men and women. It is not humility but an attribution style that files every success under 'exception'.

term: 权力让你更看不见别人的视角
oneLiner: 被“掌权”启动的人，判断他人视角时更容易把“自己看到的”当默认。
oneLinerEn: People primed with power slip toward assuming others see what they see.
detail: Galinsky 等人一系列实验发现：让受试回忆一次“自己有权”的经历后，他们在“取字视角”、“读出面部情绪”等任务上更容易把自我视角当成默认。Brion 与 Anderson 2017 的回顾进一步指出，权力同时提升目标专注、削弱“读别人”的动机——它不必然“腐败”，而是把“别人怎么想”这条通道降了权。权力越大，越需要有人专门当它的“眼睛”。
detailEn: Galinsky's team showed that recalling a time of personal power made people worse at visual perspective-taking and at reading facial emotion. Brion and Anderson (2017) added that power sharpens goal focus while dulling the motivation to model others. It does not always corrupt; it just turns the 'what do they see' channel down.

sources.label: Galinsky, Magee, Gruenfeld, Whitson & Liljenquist (2006); Brion & Anderson (2017)

term: 敬畏：看到壮阔，自我会短暂“变小”
oneLiner: 站在大峡谷前或听完一段交响乐，人会报告“自我变淡”、更愿帮忙。
oneLinerEn: Face the Grand Canyon or a great symphony, and people report a quieter 'I' and a stronger pull to help.
detail: Keltner 与海特 2003 把敬畏定义成“遇到浩瀚之物、旧有图式装不下”时的情绪；他们与后续实验发现，它常伴随“小我感”（small self）：自我评价、自恋倾向与对个人琐事的关注度短暂下降，亲社会意愿上升。Piff 等人 2015 用“站在高树上 vs 低树下”的现场实验发现，被诱导体验敬畏的受试随后愿意牺牲更多个人时间帮研究者录问卷。所谓“感动”，不只是审美体验，它是一次自我尺度的临时重设。
detailEn: Keltner and Haidt defined awe as the emotion of encountering something vast enough to strain your current schema. It tends to quiet the 'small self'—narcissistic markers dip, petty self-concern shrinks, and generosity rises. Piff's tree experiment (2015) found people standing under towering trees gave more of their time to a stranger's tedious survey.

sources.label: Keltner & Haidt (2003); Piff, Dietze, Feinberg, Stancato & Keltner (2015)

term: 数算恩典：写下五件好事，能真的拉高情绪基线
oneLiner: 每周写一次“我感激之事”，六周后幸福度与乐观都稳定上升。
oneLinerEn: A weekly 'things I'm grateful for' list nudges well-being up after six weeks.
detail: Emmons 与 McCullough 让三组受试每周分别写“感激之事”、“烦恼之事”与“中性事件”。感激组不仅自我报告的幸福度上升，还更愿运动、更少身体不适。后续元分析（Jackowska 等 2016）确认效应虽不大但稳健。它的机制并不神秘：注意被引导去搜索“已经拥有的”，而不是“缺失的”——这是“享乐适应”少被讨论的一种反向操作。
detailEn: Emmons and McCullough assigned participants to weekly lists of gratitude, hassles, or neutral events. The gratitude group reported higher well-being, exercised more and complained of fewer aches. Jackowska's 2016 meta-analysis confirmed a modest but real effect. The mechanism is attentional: the mind is set to scan for what you already have rather than what is missing.

term: 加一个更差的选项，会推高另一个“胜出”
oneLiner: 多给一个几乎没人会选的“诱饵”，能系统地把选择推向你想推的那一个。
oneLinerEn: Add an option nobody will pick and the choice tilts toward the one it is designed to lose to.
detail: 阿里里著名的《经济学人》实验：单独呈现“网络版 59 美元”与“印刷+网络 125 美元”时，多数人挑便宜的那个；加入“印刷版 125 美元”（一个明显被“支配”的选项）后，多数人改挑“印刷+网络 125 美元”——那个原本被嫌贵的选项成了对照物。偏好并不是被“内在效用”驱动，而是在呈现出来的选择之间被“关系”制造。菜单、价格表与政策框架里，都藏着这种“诱饵”。
detailEn: Ariely's Economist example: alone, 'web 59' beat 'print + web 125' for most readers. Add an apparently dominated 'print-only 125' and the target 'print + web 125' suddenly wins. Preferences are not pulled from inside; they are constructed between the options on the table. Menus, price sheets and policy frames are full of such decoys.

term: 回忆即改写：每一次取用都会重写一遍
oneLiner: 一被想起，旧的痕迹就短暂变软，容易被顺手编辑。
oneLinerEn: Every time a memory is retrieved, it briefly softens—and can be quietly edited.
detail: Nader 等 2000 在大鼠恐惧记忆中发现：被“唤起”的记忆需要新的蛋白质合成才能重新稳定，中途注射蛋白合成抑制剂会让恐惧反应永久消失——即所谓“再巩固”窗口。人类研究（Schiller 2010）显示，短时窗内改变线索可以在不消除记忆的情况下改写它的行为效应。这不只是“遗忘”，而是每一次回忆都是一次重新写入：你保留的从来不是“原件”，而是上一版草稿的最新版。
detailEn: Nader's 2000 rat study showed that a reactivated fear memory needs new protein synthesis to persist; block that process during a short window and the fear is erased. Schiller (2010) extended it to humans, altering the behavioural expression of a reactivated fear without erasing the memory itself. Recall is not playback—each retrieval re-saves the file.

sources.label: Nader, Schafe & LeDoux (2000); Schiller et al. (2010)

term: 越“别想”越想不到：抑制一个记忆会拖垮邻居
oneLiner: 主动不去想某事，会连相关的另一半也想不起来。
oneLinerEn: Suppressing one memory drags its related neighbours down with it.
detail: Anderson 与 Green 的 Think/No-Think 范式：给一个线索词，一半受试被告知“想起”对应词，一半被告知“压下去”。几十轮之后，“压制组”的目标词在自由回忆里出现率显著低于基线，甚至拖累了它同一类别的兄弟词。后续神经影像（Anderson 等 2004）显示前扣带回会向海马发出“抑制信号”。也就是说：你以为的“忘掉一件事”，其实是一次主动削弱；代价是相关的其他记忆会跟着变淡。
detailEn: In the Think/No-Think paradigm, cues told half the participants to recall a word and the other half to suppress it. After dozens of rounds the suppressed words became harder to recall than baseline—and even dragged their category-mates down. fMRI work (Anderson et al. 2004) shows anterior cingulate sending inhibitory signals to hippocampus. 'Forgetting on purpose' is real, but its blast radius is wider than intended.

term: 越挖越多：反复回忆会翻出更多旧事
oneLiner: 同一份旧材料，第二次、第三次回忆出的会比第一次还多。
oneLinerEn: Repeated recall of the same list keeps yielding items the first pass missed.
detail: Erdelyi 与 Becker 从 1974 开始的流程：让受试看一组词后连续多轮自由回忆，每轮都清零前轮的“命中”。反直觉的是—每一轮平均能新增之前几轮都想不起来的项目；轮次越多，累计召回越多。这与“提取练习”效应吻合：记忆不是一个“能/不能”的开关，而是一张会因搜索本身而更密的路径网。所谓“我全想起来了”，很多时候只是“我刚好只搜了一遍”。
detailEn: Erdelyi and Becker had participants recall the same word list round after round. Each round reliably surfaced new items that previous rounds missed—an effect they called hypermnesia. Retrieval is not a switch but a search that improves as it searches; the memory network becomes more traversable with each pass.

term: 无意识抄袭：把别人写的当成自己“灵感”
oneLiner: 想不起来的来源，容易被大脑重新贴上“我想到”的标签。
oneLinerEn: Forgotten sources get re-labelled as 'my own idea.'
detail: Marsh 与 Brown 让受试在数轮头脑风暴里既产生新点子又听到别人的点子；隔一段时间后再让他们“贡献新点子”，受试会诚实地把某条曾经听过、但已经忘了来源的点子当作“自己的原创”报告出来——这正是“潜隐记忆”（cryptomnesia）的实验室版本。它解释了为什么大量“抄袭风波”里，作者并非撒谎：当来源信息被剥离，剩下的熟悉感会被误认为原创灵感。
detailEn: In Marsh and Brown's brainstorming studies, participants honestly reported ideas they had heard weeks earlier as their own invention—once the source details faded, the residual familiarity got labelled as inspiration. This is the lab version of cryptomnesia: much accidental plagiarism isn't a lie, it's a misattribution.

term: 凹进去的面具，仍被看成凸出的脸
oneLiner: 一张从背后看是凹面具的脸，大脑会坚持把它“翻”成正脸。
oneLinerEn: Look at the inside of a mask and your brain still paints a bulging face.
detail: 从 19 世纪 Petropoulos 到 Hill 与 Bruce 1993 的复现：把一张人脸面具从内部（凹陷）朝向受试，几乎所有人在灯影下都能看到一张正常凸出的脸在跟着光源转动。Gregory 与 Ellington 1996 的机械装置表明即使有客观证据，视觉系统仍会“翻转”深度线索。近期研究（Ostaf 等 2010）显示情绪状态会影响翻转的稳定性。这不是“没看清”，而是大脑对“脸”的先验太强，压过了眼前的几何。
detailEn: Peering inside a hollow mask, almost everyone sees a bulging face rotating with the light. Gregory's mechanical version showed the effect persists even when you know the truth. Ostaf's 2010 work links resistance to flips with mood. The visual system's prior about faces overrules the geometry right in front of you.

sources.label: Hill & Bruce (1993); Gregory & Ellington (1996); Ostaf et al. (2010)

term: 随机噪声里的脸：视觉系统在过度“捕手”
oneLiner: 插座、云、汽车前脸——大脑会把偶然结构一律看成“脸”。
oneLinerEn: Outlets, clouds, car grilles—your face-detector fires on coincidental structure.
detail: 人脸检测是“过触发”的：Kanai 等 2011 用噪声图案启动让受试“看见”并不存在的脸；Ward 等 2015 的日常问卷显示大多数人在日常里都会报告这种“看到脸”。它或许源于人脸在社会认知中的极高权重——“错报有脸”几乎无成本，“漏报有脸”代价巨大。所以你在月球上找“男人”、在烤面包上找圣母，不是坏机器，而是好机器在不利的输入下过度尽职。
detailEn: Kanai's noise-priming experiments produced illusory faces; surveys find that most people report daily pareidolia. Face detection is over-triggered because missing a real face is far more costly than mistaking a wall for one. Seeing the Virgin on a piece of toast is a well-tuned detector working exactly as designed.

sources.label: Kanai et al. (2011); Ward, Li, Salivo, Vetter & Gray (2015)

term: 声音会被“抓”到眼睛那边
oneLiner: 当口型和声音只错开十几度，我们仍把声音归给“看到的嘴”。
oneLinerEn: Move the eyes 10-20° and the sound still snaps to the visible mouth.
detail: 视觉对听觉的定位有强牵引：Master 1974 让受试在偏离真实位置 10-20 度的假人头部与音频之间做判断，多数受试报告“声音从假人嘴里出来”；Howard 与 Ohlbaum 1976 的复现甚至显示他们把位置判断“重新校准”到了视觉端。这与麦格克效应是同一套跨模态先验的另一面：大脑相信“声音多半来自眼前那个东西”，所以腹语师的“错位”在感知层面真的被“掰回来了”。
detailEn: When a sound source sits 10-20° away from a visible face, listeners report the sound as coming from the face—sometimes even re-calibrating their spatial hearing. This visual capture of audition is a sibling of the McGurk effect: the brain trusts 'sound usually comes from what I'm looking at', which is exactly what ventriloquists exploit.

term: 手机幻觉震动：大腿上“叮”了一下，其实没有
oneLiner: 一半以上的智能手机用户报告过“手机在震”，但根本没震。
oneLinerEn: Most smartphone users report a buzz that never happened.
detail: Roth 等 2012 的问卷显示接近九成受访医学生至少有过一次“幻震”；Eckert 等 2012 更把这一现象与“幻痒”归到“内感受预测”框架：当身体与设备长时间共构，大脑会把轻微肌肉颤动“解释”成手机震动——它不是“错觉”，而是“感知推断”的一次高置信度失误。所谓“手机长在身上”，其实是一次感官层的耦合。
detailEn: Roth's survey found nearly 90% of medical students had felt a phone vibrate when it did not. Eckert's group reframes it as interoceptive prediction: once the body co-models the device, small muscle twitches get explained as phone buzzes. It is not a glitch; it is a high-confidence inference going slightly wrong.

sources.label: Roth, Coen, Eisen & Wilken (2012); Eckert et al. (2012)

term: 旁观者效应：越多人在场，越少人伸手
oneLiner: 有人倒下的街上，人越多，越晚有人报警。
oneLinerEn: The more witnesses to a collapse, the longer before anyone acts.
detail: Kitty Genovese 传闻点燃了这项研究；Latané 与 Darley 1968 让受试在隔间里通过对讲机听到有人癫痫发作——独处时 85% 的人在下一次机会前出手帮忙，而以为还有其他 4 人在场时只有 31%。近年元分析（Fischer 等 2011）指出在紧急情况且情境含糊时效应最强。这不是“城市冷漠”，而是责任的算术：多一个人就多一份“他会打的”。
detailEn: Latané and Darley's seizure-intercom study: alone, 85% of listeners intervened; believing four others also heard, only 31% did. Fischer's 2011 meta-analysis confirms it peaks when the situation is ambiguous. Not urban coldness—a diffusion-of-responsibility arithmetic: one more witness is one more 'surely they'll call'.

term: 团体迷思：一群人越一致，越容易做出荒唐决定
oneLiner: 凝聚力越高、越“咱们都是自己人”，坏消息越容易被封在门外。
oneLinerEn: The tighter the team, the better at locking bad news out.
detail: Janis 用猪湾事件、珍珠港预警等案例提出“团体迷思”：内群体压力让成员自我审查疑虑、把异议解释成“不忠诚”，最终做出任何单人都不太可能选出的错决定。虽然后续案例研究有方法论争议（Kroon & Van Glas 等 2017 复现有限），但“共同决策里，沉默会被当作同意”这一机制在商业、陪审团与政策中被反复报告。真正的解药不是“多讨论”，而是有人被授权公开唱反调。
detailEn: Janis traced a pattern in the Bay of Pigs and Pearl Harbor: cohesive groups self-censor doubts and read dissent as disloyalty, arriving at choices no individual member would have made alone. Later replications are mixed, but the mechanism—silence read as agreement—shows up in boardrooms, juries and policy rooms. The fix is not more talk but a designated dissenter.

term: 光环效应：一处好，处处都好
oneLiner: 长相有魅力的人被系统性评为更聪明、更诚信、更适合当领导。
oneLinerEn: Attractive people are rated smarter, more honest and better leader-material—without evidence.
detail: Thorndike 1920 让上级对士兵多维度打分，发现各维度之间相关性远高于独立评价应有的水平，第一次命名了“光环”。Nisbett 与 Wilson 1977 让学生看同一位讲师的两段视频（各自人格化处理）后，学生对讲师“外貌是否吸引人”的评价几乎预测了他们对“讲课内容质量”、“生活习惯”的评分——尽管他们否认外貌影响了判断。所谓“独立评分”，很多时候只是一份好看的外推。
detailEn: Thorndike's army ratings showed cross-dimension correlation too high for independent judgments. Nisbett and Wilson's video study: whether students found a lecturer attractive predicted their ratings of his content, even as they denied any influence. Independent-sounding ratings are often extrapolations from one salient trait.

term: 最小群体：只因为分组，就开始偏心
oneLiner: 让受试投硬币分“红/蓝队”，几分钟他们就系统性偏袒“自己队”。
oneLinerEn: Coin-toss 'teams' get systematic favouritism within minutes.
detail: Tajfel 1971 让布里斯托的中学男生玩一个刻意“没有任何理由”的分组游戏——有人被随机分成 K 组、有人被分成 A 组；随后让他们在两份陌生人的奖金分配表上做决定。结果显示即使分组只是随机字母、成员之间从未见面，“给本组多分”依然是主流选择。这个“最小群体范式”说明：偏见并不需要历史冲突、经济利益、外貌差异——只需要一条“我们/他们”的线。
detailEn: Tajfel split schoolboys into groups by nothing more than a coin toss, then asked them to allocate rewards between anonymous in-group and out-group members. Favouritism appeared instantly. Bigotry requires no real conflict—only a line between 'us' and 'them'.

term: 俄语有两种“蓝”，说俄语的人分得更快
oneLiner: 有独立浅蓝与深蓝基本色词的俄语者，辨别相近蓝色时反应更快。
oneLinerEn: Speakers of Russian, which splits light and dark blue into separate basic colour terms, discriminate shades faster.
detail: Winawer 与 Boroditsky 等 2007 的实验中，受试看三色块找不同。俄语者在浅蓝 голубой 与深蓝 синий 跳类别时的辨别速度显著快于英语者；且当同时让受试做语言干扰任务时，这个优势消失，视觉搜索任务则不受影响。这不意味着“俄语者眼睛不一样”，而是“词汇在合适的时机搭了把手”。语言相对论第一次拿到了反应时级别的可控证据。
detailEn: Russian speakers were quicker than English speakers at discriminating light vs dark blue across the голубой/синий boundary, and the advantage vanished under a verbal (but not spatial) secondary task. Not a different eye—a word that lends a hand at the right moment. It was the first reaction-time-grade evidence for linguistic relativity.

term: 学会阅读，重塑你的视觉皮层
oneLiner: 识字者的枕颞叶出现一个专门给“字”的分区，且白质束也随之变粗。
oneLinerEn: Literacy carves a visual word-form area and thickens the white matter feeding language.
detail: Dehaene 与 Cohen 的系列 fMRI 工作发现，人在学会阅读后，左侧枕-颞叶会出现一个专门对字母串反应的区域——“视觉词形区”。同一支团队 2010 年在《自然·神经科学》上比较巴西成年文盲与识字者：识字不仅增强 VWFA，还让通往语言区的白质束显著更粗，且这种改变在文盲成人被“夜校”教会读写的六个月后已经出现。所谓“读书让人变聪明”，很可能有神经解剖层面的直接证据。
detailEn: Dehaene and Cohen's group identified a Visual Word Form Area that lights up once you learn to read. Comparing illiterate and literate Brazilians, they showed literacy thickens not just VWFA but the white-matter tracts to language regions—and six months of adult literacy classes already moves the needle. Reading literally reshapes the brain.

term: “现在”只有大约 3 秒
termEn: The Specious Present Is About 3 Seconds
oneLiner: 音乐乐句、对话轮次、意识“当下”，都被约 3 秒的窗口框住。
oneLinerEn: Musical phrases, conversational turns, and consciousness' 'now' all sit inside a ~3-second window.
detail: Pöppel 1997 汇总多项心理物理与神经影像证据：知觉组织、短时记忆、语言韵律、音乐曲式的“自然断点”都稳定落在 2-4 秒之间，他把这段“活的现在”称为 specious present。后续工作把它和“事件分割”（Zacks 与 Tversky 2001）与工作记忆的时间约束挂钩。也就是说，你以为是“连续的一段”，其实是被大脑按 ~3 秒切帧重播；这也解释了为什么音乐副歌、讲笑话的“铺垫→抖包袱”、甚至思考的“下一句”，都天然在这个尺度上呼吸。
detailEn: Pöppel's synthesis: perception, working memory, prosody, and musical phrasing all cluster around 2-4 seconds. Later work ties this to event segmentation (Zacks & Tversky 2001). What feels like a continuous 'now' is actually sliced at ~3-second intervals—which is why jokes, choruses, and thought-units all breathe at that scale.

term: 眼跳前，时间被“压缩”
termEn: Time Compresses Before Your Eyes Move
oneLiner: 就在眼球跳动的瞬间之前，视觉事件会显得更早、更短。
oneLinerEn: In the milliseconds before a saccade, events appear earlier and shorter.
detail: 眼跳并不是简单的“相机切换”：Burr、Ross 与 Bridgeman 1981 让受试在扫视前看到闪光，他们会把闪光定位到即将落点的方向；Morrone、Ross 与 Burr 1982 又发现受试判断“事件持续时间”时，眼跳前的时间会被压缩到实际的一半以下。这与“眼跳抑制”（我们看不见眼球转动本身）配套，说明大脑为了维持视觉连续感，会主动对时间做手术——你之所以“没注意到”，是因为它根本没让你看到那段。
detailEn: Before a saccade, flashes are mislocalised toward the future eye position, and their duration shrinks—part of a broader surgery that lets us experience vision as continuous despite constant jumps. You don't see the saccade because time itself gets edited out.

sources.label: Burr, Ross & Bridgeman (1981); Morrone, Ross & Burr (1982)

term: fMRI 比你早 7 秒“知道”你要按哪个键
termEn: Brain Predicts Your Choice Up to 7 Seconds Early
oneLiner: 从额极与内侧顶叶活动可以提前数秒解码出受试“随意”按左还是右。
oneLinerEn: Frontopolar and parietal activity predicts a supposedly free button press seconds before awareness.
detail: Soon 等 2008 在《自然·神经科学》让受试“任意时候”按下左或右按钮，同时记录 fMRI。事后模型可以从额极（BA10）与内侧顶叶的活动里，在受试报告“决定了”之前最多约 7.5 秒就解码出选择，命中率约 60%（看似不多，但对 50% 基线是显著）。作者本人明确说这不等于“决定已被写死”，而是把决策的神经前因往前推。它挑战的不是自由意志是否存在，而是“我意识到的时刻就是决定的开始”这一时间感。
detailEn: Soon et al. decoded a supposedly free left/right button choice from frontopolar and parietal activity up to 7.5 seconds before reported awareness, with about 60% accuracy against a 50% baseline. The authors were clear: this is not proof of determinism. What it undermines is the intuition that awareness marks the start of the decision.

term: 深部脑刺激开机那一刻，人的价值观也会跟着漂
termEn: Deep Brain Stimulation Shifts Values on Switch-On
oneLiner: 电极一通电，帕金森患者的风险偏好、道德判断甚至“人生的意义感”会短期偏移。
oneLinerEn: Flip the current on and risk appetite, moral judgements, and sense of meaning can drift.
detail: Schübler 等 2009 让帕金森患者在自己的 DBS 开关开/关两种状态下做道德两难判断：开机时的“不可接受行为”判定阈值显著移动。Rudenko 等 2012 与 Korf 的回顾都指出，DBS 有时伴随“我好像不是我了”的自述。这一系列发现把“我做的选择”从“我的性格”上短暂剥离——电极下几毫米的电流就能改变道德判断，让我们更小心地谈“这就是我”。
detailEn: Schübler's 2009 study found Parkinson patients judged moral dilemmas differently with their stimulator switched on. Rudenko (2012) and Korf's review describe a 'not-me' feeling in some cases. A few millimetres of current can shift moral thresholds, which counsels caution with the phrase 'this is who I am'.

term: 教新手的“详细示例”，会拖累专家的学习
oneLiner: 同样一份分步骤讲解，对新手有效、对老手反而更差。
oneLinerEn: Step-by-step worked examples help novices but hurt experts learning the next topic.
detail: Kalyuga、Ayres、Chandler 与 Sweller 2003：给新手看“完整解题示范”显著提升后续独立解题；但把同样精细的示范给已经熟练的学生，成绩反而下降。原因被归入“认知负荷”框架：专家已内化的图式被冗余信息“覆写”，反而占用工作记忆。这条效应提醒：好的教学法不是“越多细节越好”，而是随学习者能力逐步拆脚手架——把“必要难度”和“信息冗余”分开。
detailEn: Full worked examples boosted novices but hurt advanced learners on the next topic (Kalyuga et al. 2003). The redundancy forces experts to re-process information they already know, eating working-memory budget. Good teaching scaffolds in and out with skill—a close cousin of desirable difficulties.
